source.text: Τί οὖν τὸ περισσὸν τοῦ Ἰουδαίου, ἢ τίς ἡ ὠφέλεια τῆς περιτομῆς;

records.literal_gloss: What then the advantage of the Jew, or what the benefit of the circumcision?

en.L: What then [is] the advantage of the Jew, or what [is] the benefit of circumcision?
en.B: Then what advantage does the Jew have? What good is circumcision?
en.R: So is there any advantage in being a Jew? Does circumcision do any good?

es.L: ¿Cuál [es], pues, la ventaja del judío, o cuál [es] el provecho de la circuncisión?
es.B: Entonces, ¿qué ventaja tiene el judío? ¿De qué sirve la circuncisión?
es.R: Entonces, ¿hay alguna ventaja en ser judío? ¿Sirve de algo la circuncisión?

fr.L: Qu’[a] donc de plus le Juif, ou quel [est] le profit de la circoncision ?
fr.B: Alors, quel avantage le Juif a-t-il ? À quoi sert la circoncision ?
fr.R: Alors, est-ce qu’il y a un avantage à être juif ? Est-ce que la circoncision sert à quelque chose ?

sw.L: Basi, [ni] nini ubora wa Myahudi, au [ni] nini faida ya tohara?
sw.B: Basi, Myahudi ana ubora gani? Tohara ina manufaa gani?
sw.R: Basi, je, kuna faida yoyote kuwa Myahudi? Je, tohara inasaidia chochote?

decisions.reason: If the true Jew is the one who is a Jew inwardly, a listener may ask whether being a Jew by birth means anything. Paul raises the question himself and answers it.
περισσός is what is more than others have, an advantage or privilege.

source.text: πολὺ κατὰ πάντα τρόπον.

records.literal_gloss: Much in every way.

en.L: Much in every way.
en.B: Much, in every way.
en.R: There is a great advantage in every way.

es.L: Mucho, en todo sentido.
es.B: Mucha, en todos los sentidos.
es.R: Hay una gran ventaja en todos los sentidos.

fr.L: Beaucoup, de toute manière.
fr.B: Il est grand, à tous égards.
fr.R: Oui, il y a un grand avantage, à tous points de vue.

sw.L: Mwingi kwa kila namna.
sw.B: Ni mwingi, kwa kila hali.
sw.R: Kuna faida kubwa kwa kila namna.

source.text: πρῶτον μὲν γὰρ ὅτι ἐπιστεύθησαν τὰ λόγια τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: First indeed for that they were entrusted the oracles of the God.

en.L: For first, they were entrusted with the oracles of God.
en.B: To begin with, the Jews were entrusted with the very words of God.
en.R: First of all, God gave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words to the Jews and trusted them to keep them.

es.L: Porque, en primer lugar, les fueron confiados los oráculos de Dios.
es.B: Para empezar, a los judíos se les confiaron las palabras mismas de Dios.
es.R: Ante todo, Dios dio {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} palabras a los judíos y les confió el cuidado de ellas.

fr.L: Car en premier lieu, ils se sont vu confier les oracles de Dieu.
fr.B: Tout d’abord, les Juifs ont reçu en dépôt les paroles mêmes de Dieu.
fr.R: D’abord, Dieu a donné {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} paroles aux Juifs, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a fait confiance pour les garder.

sw.L: Kwa maana kwanza, waliaminiwa kauli za Mungu.
sw.B: Kwanza kabisa, Wayahudi waliaminiwa maneno yenyewe ya Mungu.
sw.R: Kwanza, Mungu aliwapa Wayahudi maneno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, akawaamini kwamba watayatunza.

decisions.reason: πιστεύω usually means to believe or trust. In the passive with an object it means to be entrusted with something, as Paul says he was entrusted with the gospel (1 Thessalonians 2:4).

decisions.choice: the oracles of God: God's spoken words, the Scriptures
decisions.reason: λόγιον is a divine saying. Here it is what God said to Israel in the Scriptures, above all his promises. The verbs that follow play on this: entrusted, unfaithful, faithfulness.

decisions.choice: first: the list is not finished
decisions.reason: As in 1:8, "first" has no "second". Paul gives the full list of Israel's privileges in 9:4-5.

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives ("maneno yake")
alternatives: a span for every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: As in Romans 1:1, Swahili marks most pronouns for God inside the verb ("aliwapa", "akawaamini"), where a capital is impossible, so the deity_pronoun setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, and this chapter has fewer spans than the English.

"Kuaminiwa" (to be trusted with) is the passive of "kuamini", as the Greek verb is the passive of "believe". It keeps the play the meaning decision points out with "waaminifu" and "uaminifu" in verse 3; "kukabidhiwa" (to be handed over) is plainer but loses the link. Readable says it plainly: God gave them his words and trusted them ("akawaamini") to keep them.

source.text: τί γάρ;

records.literal_gloss: What for?

en.L: For what [then]?
en.B: What of it?
en.R: So what does that mean?

es.L: Pues ¿qué [entonces]?
es.B: ¿Y qué?
es.R: Entonces, ¿qué significa eso?

fr.L: Car quoi [donc] ?
fr.B: Qu’importe ?
fr.R: Alors, qu’est-ce que cela veut dire ?

sw.L: Kwa maana [ni] nini [basi]?
sw.B: Basi, je?
sw.R: Basi, hiyo ina maana gani?

decisions.reason: A short spoken question, "what then?", introducing the next objection.

source.text: εἰ ἠπίστησάν τινες, μὴ ἡ ἀπιστία αὐτῶν τὴν πίστιν τοῦ θεοῦ καταργήσει;

records.literal_gloss: If disbelieved some, not the unbelief of them the faithfulness of the God will nullify?

en.L: If some were unfaithful, their unfaithfulness will not nullify the faithfulness of God, will it?
en.B: If some were unfaithful, does their unfaithfulness cancel out God's faithfulness?
en.R: Some of them were not faithful to God. Does that mean God will not be faithful to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promises?

es.L: Si algunos fueron infieles, su infidelidad no anulará la fidelidad de Dios, ¿verdad?
es.B: Si algunos fueron infieles, ¿acaso su infidelidad deja sin efecto la fidelidad de Dios?
es.R: Algunos de ellos no fueron fieles a Dios. ¿Quiere decir eso que Dios no será fiel a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} promesas?

fr.L: Si certains ont été infidèles, leur infidélité ne va tout de même pas annuler la fidélité de Dieu ?
fr.B: Si certains ont été infidèles, leur infidélité réduit-elle à rien la fidélité de Dieu ?
fr.R: Certains d’entre eux n’ont pas été fidèles à Dieu. Est-ce que cela veut dire que Dieu ne sera pas fidèle à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} promesses ?

sw.L: Ikiwa baadhi hawakuwa waaminifu, kutokuwa kwao waaminifu hakutaubatilisha uaminifu wa Mungu, sivyo?
sw.B: Ikiwa baadhi yao hawakuwa waaminifu, je, kutokuwa kwao waaminifu kunaubatilisha uaminifu wa Mungu?
sw.R: Baadhi yao hawakuwa waaminifu kwa Mungu. Je, hiyo inamaanisha kwamba Mungu hatakuwa mwaminifu kwa ahadi {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}?

decisions.reason: πίστις is usually faith, but used of God it is his faithfulness, his keeping of what he promised (the oracles of verse 2).

ἀπιστέω and ἀπιστία can mean unbelief or unfaithfulness. Set against God's faithfulness, and after "entrusted", the point is that some of Israel did not keep faith with what was entrusted to them; this includes not believing the gospel (10:16, 11:20).

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: The question begins with μὴ, which expects "no".

The settled word for this noun is "fe", but said of God it means his faithfulness, as the meaning decision explains, so Spanish says "fidelidad". The human side follows: "infieles" and "infidelidad" (not keeping faith) rather than "incredulidad" (unbelief), so the contrast with God's "fidelidad" stays visible. "Infidelidad" often means unfaithfulness in marriage; the context makes the sense clear, but a reviewer may prefer "falta de fidelidad".

decisions.choice: "ne … tout de même pas … ?" for a question that expects the answer no (here and in 3:5)
decisions.reason: The Greek marks the question as expecting "no" (m3). English Literal adds "will it?"; French says it inside the question with "tout de même", which keeps the Greek order.

Said of God the word means faithfulness (meaning decision), so Swahili says "uaminifu" rather than the settled "imani", and the human side is "kutokuwa waaminifu" (not being faithful). "Uaminifu", "waaminifu", "imani" and "kuamini" share one root, so the play on "waliaminiwa" (entrusted, verse 2), unfaithful and faithfulness stays audible, as it is in Greek.

source.text: μὴ γένοιτο· γινέσθω δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἀληθής, πᾶς δὲ ἄνθρωπος ψεύστης, καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὅπως ἂν δικαιωθῇς ἐν τοῖς λόγοις σου καὶ νικήσεις ἐν τῷ κρίνεσθαί σε.

records.literal_gloss: May it not be; let be and the God true, every and man a liar, as it has been written: That you may be justified in the words of you and will prevail in the to be judged you.

en.L: May it not be! But let God be true, and every {{gender:human being|man}} a liar, just as it is written, "So that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} may be justified in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words and prevail when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are judged."
en.B: Certainly not! Let God be found true, even if every human being is a liar. As it is written, "So that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are shown to be right when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} speak, and win {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} case when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are judged."
en.R: Of course not! God always tells the truth, even if every person is a liar. The Scriptures say this to God: "You are right in what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will win when people judge {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

es.L: ¡No sea así! Antes bien, sea Dios veraz, y todo {{gender:ser humano|hombre}} mentiroso, así como está escrito: «Para que seas justificado en {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} palabras y venzas cuando {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} seas juzgado».
es.B: ¡De ningún modo! Que Dios resulte veraz, aunque todo ser humano sea mentiroso. Como está escrito: «Para que se vea que tienes razón cuando hablas, y ganes {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} causa cuando {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} juzguen».
es.R: ¡Claro que no! Dios siempre dice la verdad, aunque toda persona sea mentirosa. Las Escrituras le dicen a Dios: «Tienes razón en lo que dices, y cuando la gente {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} juzgue, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} ganarás».

fr.L: Qu’il n’en soit rien ! Mais que Dieu soit vrai, et tout {{gender:être humain|homme}} menteur, selon qu’il est écrit : « Afin que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sois justifié dans {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} paroles et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’emportes quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es jugé. »
fr.B: Certainement pas ! Que Dieu soit reconnu vrai, même si tout être humain est menteur. Comme il est écrit : « Afin que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sois reconnu juste quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} parles, et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gagnes {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cause quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es jugé. »
fr.R: Bien sûr que non ! Dieu dit toujours la vérité, même si tout le monde ment. Les Écritures disent ceci à Dieu : « Tu as raison dans ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} dis, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gagneras quand les gens {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} jugeront. »

sw.L: Isiwe hivyo! Bali Mungu awe wa kweli, na kila mwanadamu mwongo, kama ilivyoandikwa, "Ili uhesabiwe haki katika maneno {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, na ushinde unapohukumiwa."
sw.B: Hasha! Mungu na aonekane kuwa wa kweli, hata kama kila mwanadamu ni mwongo. Kama ilivyoandikwa, "Ili uonekane kuwa mwenye haki unaposema, na ushinde kesi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} unapohukumiwa."
sw.R: Sivyo kabisa! Mungu husema kweli daima, hata kama kila mtu ni mwongo. Maandiko yanamwambia Mungu hivi: "Uko sahihi katika maneno {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, na utashinda watu watakapokuhukumu."

decisions.reason: μή in this form is a wish, "may it not come to be". Paul uses it to reject a false conclusion outright.

decisions.choice: every human being a liar: Psalm 116:11
decisions.reason: "Every man is a liar" is from Psalm 116:11. Whoever proves false, God stays true.
The quotation is from Psalm 51:6, in the wording of the Greek translation (Psalm 50:6 in its numbering). There David confesses his sin and says that God is right to judge him.
The form can be passive ("when you are judged", as if God were taken to court) or middle ("when you judge"). The picture of God winning his case fits the passive.

decisions.choice: May it not be! / Certainly not! / Of course not!
decisions.reason: Paul's strongest no, literally "may it not happen". The same English is used at each level wherever Romans has it (as in 9:14 and 11:1).
The word means a human being, man or woman.
Pronouns addressed to God.

decisions.choice: ¡No sea así! (L); ¡De ningún modo! (B); ¡Claro que no! (R)
decisions.reason: As in 11:1, the same Spanish is used at each level wherever Romans has Paul's strongest no: here and in verses 6 and 31.

decisions.choice: se vea que tienes razón (B); tienes razón (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "justificar", the settled word for this verb. Here God is the one "justified": he is shown to be in the right when he speaks, as in the psalm, not declared righteous as a sinner is. Balanced and Readable say that, as the English does, so that the settled term is not misread.

The quotation speaks to God. Spanish shows "you" mostly in the verb ending, which cannot take a capital, so the setting marks the free pronouns and possessives, and Literal and Readable add "tú" once so the subject can carry it.

decisions.choice: Qu’il n’en soit rien ! (L); Certainement pas ! (B); Bien sûr que non ! (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: Paul's strongest no (m1). Each level uses the same French wherever Romans has it (3:6, 3:31, 6:2, 7:7, 11:1), as the English does. Literal keeps the wish form of the Greek; Balanced and Readable say it as a French speaker would.
As the style guide has it, God is addressed with "tu", and each pronoun addressed to him carries the span wherever the English "you" does; a "Tu" that opens the quoted sentence is written plainly.
As in 11:1, the same Swahili is used at each level wherever Romans has Paul's strongest no: here and in verses 6 and 31.

decisions.choice: uhesabiwe haki (L); uonekane kuwa mwenye haki (B); uko sahihi (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "kuhesabiwa haki", the settled verb. Here God is the one "justified": he is shown to be in the right when he speaks, not counted righteous as a sinner is. Balanced says "uonekane kuwa mwenye haki" (be seen to be in the right) and Readable "uko sahihi" (you are right), as the English does.
As in 2:1, "mwanadamu" is a human being, man or woman, so the English gender setting has nothing to change in Swahili, here or in verse 28.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ἡ ἀδικία ἡμῶν θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην συνίστησιν, τί ἐροῦμεν;

records.literal_gloss: If but the unrighteousness of us God's righteousness shows, what will we say?

en.L: But if our unrighteousness shows God's righteousness, what will we say?
en.B: But if our wrongdoing brings out God's righteousness more clearly, what are we to say?
en.R: But suppose the wrong things we do make it clearer that God is righteous. What should we say then?

es.L: Pero si nuestra injusticia hace resaltar la justicia de Dios, ¿qué diremos?
es.B: Pero si nuestra injusticia pone más de relieve la justicia de Dios, ¿qué vamos a decir?
es.R: Pero supongamos que nuestra injusticia deja más claro que Dios es justo. ¿Qué diremos entonces?

fr.L: Mais si notre injustice met en évidence la justice de Dieu, que dirons-nous ?
fr.B: Mais si le mal que nous faisons fait ressortir plus clairement la justice de Dieu, que devons-nous dire ?
fr.R: Mais imaginons que le mal que nous faisons montre plus clairement que Dieu est juste. Que faut-il dire alors ?

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa kutokuwa kwetu na haki kunaonyesha haki ya Mungu, tutasema nini?
sw.B: Lakini ikiwa kutokuwa kwetu na haki kunaifanya haki ya Mungu ionekane wazi zaidi, tuseme nini?
sw.R: Lakini tuchukulie kwamba mabaya tunayotenda yanaonyesha wazi zaidi kwamba Mungu ni mwenye haki. Tuseme nini basi?

decisions.reason: συνίστημι is to show or make plain; human wrongdoing makes God's righteousness stand out by contrast.
The two words share a root: our lack of righteousness against God's righteousness, as in 1:17-18.

decisions.choice: wrongdoing; the wrong things we do
decisions.reason: As in 1:18.

As in 1:18, Spanish "injusticia" is both the plain word and the opposite of "justicia", so every level keeps the pair the meaning decision points out, where English Balanced and Readable say "wrongdoing".

The meaning decision stresses that the two words share a root. "Kutokuwa na haki" (not having righteousness) keeps "haki" in both, so Literal and Balanced use it here rather than "udhalimu"; Readable says "mabaya tunayotenda" (the wrong we do), as the English Readable does.

source.text: μὴ ἄδικος ὁ θεὸς ὁ ἐπιφέρων τὴν ὀργήν;

records.literal_gloss: Not unrighteous the God the [one] bringing on the wrath?

en.L: God, who brings wrath, is not unrighteous, is he?
en.B: Is God unjust, then, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wrath on us?
en.R: Is God unfair when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} punishes us in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger?

es.L: Dios, que trae la ira, no es injusto, ¿verdad?
es.B: ¿Es injusto Dios, entonces, cuando descarga {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira sobre nosotros?
es.R: ¿Es Dios injusto cuando nos castiga con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira?

fr.L: Dieu, qui inflige la colère, n’est tout de même pas injuste ?
fr.B: Dieu est-il donc injuste quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fait tomber {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère sur nous ?
fr.R: Dieu est-il injuste quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous punit dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère ?

sw.L: Mungu aletaye ghadhabu si dhalimu, sivyo?
sw.B: Je, basi, Mungu ni dhalimu anapoleta ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} juu yetu?
sw.R: Je, Mungu anatutendea isivyo haki anapotuadhibu kwa ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}?

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, the question expects "no": the objector puts it in a cautious form.
ἄδικος is the adjective of the word for unrighteousness: is God in the wrong when he judges?
As in 1:18.
As in 1:18, Spanish "ira" is an everyday word, so Readable keeps the key term where the English Readable says "anger".

"Hana haki" would also be heard as "has no right". "Dhalimu" (unjust, one who wrongs others) asks plainly whether God does wrong when he judges; Readable says "anatutendea isivyo haki" (treats us unjustly), which keeps "haki". "Ghadhabu" stays at every level for God's wrath.

source.text: κατὰ ἄνθρωπον λέγω.

records.literal_gloss: According to man I speak.

en.L: I speak according to [a] human [way of thinking].
en.B: I am speaking as people do.
en.R: I am talking the way people talk.

es.L: Hablo según [un modo] humano.
es.B: Hablo como habla la gente.
es.R: Hablo como lo haría cualquier persona.

fr.L: Je parle selon [une façon de penser] humaine.
fr.B: Je parle comme le font les gens.
fr.R: Je parle comme parlent les gens.

sw.L: Nasema kwa kadiri ya [mawazo ya] kibinadamu.
sw.B: Ninasema kama wanadamu wasemavyo.
sw.R: Ninazungumza jinsi watu wanavyozungumza.

decisions.choice: I am using a human argument
decisions.reason: Paul marks the question as the kind of reasoning people use, which he does not share (6:19, Galatians 3:15).

source.text: μὴ γένοιτο· ἐπεὶ πῶς κρινεῖ ὁ θεὸς τὸν κόσμον;

records.literal_gloss: May it not be; otherwise how will judge the God the world?

en.L: May it not be! Otherwise how will God judge the world?
en.B: Certainly not! If that were so, how could God judge the world?
en.R: Of course not! If God were unfair, how could {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} judge the world?

es.L: ¡No sea así! De otro modo, ¿cómo juzgará Dios al mundo?
es.B: ¡De ningún modo! Si así fuera, ¿cómo podría Dios juzgar al mundo?
es.R: ¡Claro que no! Si Dios fuera injusto, ¿cómo podría juzgar al mundo?

fr.L: Qu’il n’en soit rien ! Autrement, comment Dieu jugera-t-il le monde ?
fr.B: Certainement pas ! S’il en était ainsi, comment Dieu pourrait-il juger le monde ?
fr.R: Bien sûr que non ! Si Dieu était injuste, comment pourrait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} juger le monde ?

sw.L: Isiwe hivyo! La sivyo, Mungu atauhukumu ulimwengu jinsi gani?
sw.B: Hasha! Kama ingekuwa hivyo, Mungu angewezaje kuuhukumu ulimwengu?
sw.R: Sivyo kabisa! Kama Mungu angekuwa dhalimu, angewezaje kuuhukumu ulimwengu?

decisions.reason: μή in this form is a wish, "may it not come to be". Paul uses it to reject a false conclusion outright.

decisions.choice: God is the judge of the world
decisions.reason: That God will judge the world was common ground for Paul and his listeners (Genesis 18:25). If he were unjust, he could not be its judge.

decisions.choice: May it not be! / Certainly not! / Of course not!
decisions.reason: Paul's strongest no, literally "may it not happen". The same English is used at each level wherever Romans has it (as in 9:14 and 11:1).

source.text: εἰ δὲ ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ ψεύσματι ἐπερίσσευσεν εἰς τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, τί ἔτι κἀγὼ ὡς ἁμαρτωλὸς κρίνομαι, καὶ μὴ καθὼς βλασφημούμεθα καὶ καθώς φασίν τινες ἡμᾶς λέγειν ὅτι Ποιήσωμεν τὰ κακὰ ἵνα ἔλθῃ τὰ ἀγαθά;

records.literal_gloss: If but the truth of the God in the my lie abounded to the glory of him, why still also I as sinner am judged, \v 8 and not, as we are slandered and as say some us to say that: Let us do the evil [things] that may come the good [things]?

en.L: But if through my lie the truth of God has abounded to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, why am I still being judged as a sinner? \v 8 And why not [say], as we are slandered and as some claim that we say, "Let us do evil things so that good things may come"?
en.B: But if my falsehood makes God's truth shine out all the more, to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, why am I, too, still judged a sinner? \v 8 And why not do what some slander us by saying we teach: "Let us do evil so that good may come of it"?
en.R: Someone might say, "When I lie, it shows even more clearly that God tells the truth, and that brings {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory. So why does God still judge me as a sinner?" \v 8 Then why not say, "Let us do evil so that good will come from it"? Some people tell lies about us and say that this is what we teach.

es.L: Pero si por mi mentira la verdad de Dios abundó para {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria, ¿por qué todavía soy juzgado yo también como pecador? \v 8 ¿Y por qué no [decir], como se nos calumnia y como algunos afirman que decimos: «Hagamos las cosas malas para que vengan las buenas»?
es.B: Pero si mi falsedad hace brillar aún más la verdad de Dios, para {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria, ¿por qué se me sigue juzgando a mí también como pecador? \v 8 ¿Y por qué no hacer lo que algunos, calumniándonos, dicen que enseñamos: «Hagamos el mal para que de ello salga el bien»?
es.R: Alguien podría decir: «Cuando miento, se ve aún más claro que Dios dice la verdad, y eso {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} da gloria. Entonces, ¿por qué Dios todavía me juzga como pecador?». \v 8 Entonces, ¿por qué no decir: «Hagamos el mal para que venga el bien»? Algunas personas mienten sobre nosotros y dicen que eso es lo que enseñamos.

fr.L: Mais si, par mon mensonge, la vérité de Dieu a abondé pour {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire, pourquoi suis-je encore, moi aussi, jugé comme pécheur ? \v 8 Et pourquoi ne [dirions-nous] pas, comme on nous calomnie et comme certains prétendent que nous [le] disons : « Faisons le mal pour que vienne le bien » ?
fr.B: Mais si mon mensonge fait briller davantage la vérité de Dieu, pour {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire, pourquoi suis-je, moi aussi, encore jugé comme pécheur ? \v 8 Et pourquoi ne pas faire ce que, selon certains qui nous calomnient, nous enseignons : « Faisons le mal pour qu’il en sorte du bien » ?
fr.R: Quelqu’un pourrait dire : « Quand je mens, cela montre encore plus clairement que Dieu dit la vérité, et cela {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} donne de la gloire. Alors pourquoi Dieu me juge-t-il encore comme un pécheur ? » \v 8 Alors pourquoi ne pas dire : « Faisons le mal pour qu’il en sorte du bien » ? Certaines personnes mentent à notre sujet et disent que c’est ce que nous enseignons.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa kweli ya Mungu imezidi kwa uongo wangu kwa ajili ya utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, kwa nini mimi pia bado ninahukumiwa kama mwenye dhambi? \v 8 Na kwa nini [tusiseme], kama tunavyosingiziwa na kama wengine wanavyodai kwamba tunasema, "Na tutende mabaya ili mema yaje"?
sw.B: Lakini ikiwa uongo wangu unaifanya kweli ya Mungu ionekane wazi zaidi, kwa utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, kwa nini mimi pia bado ninahukumiwa kuwa mwenye dhambi? \v 8 Na kwa nini tusifanye kama wengine wanavyotusingizia kwamba tunafundisha: "Tutende maovu ili mema yatokee"?
sw.R: Mtu anaweza kusema, "Ninaposema uongo, inaonekana wazi zaidi kwamba Mungu husema kweli, na hilo linampa utukufu. Basi kwa nini Mungu bado ananihukumu kama mwenye dhambi?" \v 8 Basi kwa nini tusiseme, "Tutende mabaya ili mema yaje"? Watu wengine wanatusingizia na kusema kwamba hivyo ndivyo tunavyofundisha.

decisions.reason: Paul voices the objection in the first person, as anyone might put it.

decisions.choice: God's truth against my lie: his faithfulness against human falseness
decisions.reason: Truth here is God's truthfulness, his being true to his word, as in verse 4. It stands with his faithfulness (verse 3) and righteousness (verse 5).
Verse 8 starts a second question and breaks off into a quotation of what Paul's opponents say he teaches.

decisions.choice: Paul's teaching on grace was misrepresented
decisions.reason: Some said that Paul's gospel of grace without works of the law encouraged sin. He answers the charge again in 6:1 and 6:15.
Readable marks the objection as someone else's words, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: ὧν τὸ κρίμα ἔνδικόν ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Of whom the condemnation just is.

en.L: Their condemnation is just.
en.B: Such people deserve their condemnation.
en.R: God will be right to condemn people like that.

es.L: La condenación de ellos es justa.
es.B: Esos tienen bien merecida su condenación.
es.R: Dios hará bien en condenar a gente así.

fr.L: Leur condamnation est juste.
fr.B: Ces gens-là méritent leur condamnation.
fr.R: Dieu aura raison de condamner de tels gens.

sw.L: Ambao kuhukumiwa kwao ni kwa haki.
sw.B: Watu kama hao wanastahili kuhukumiwa.
sw.R: Mungu atatenda haki akiwahukumu watu wa namna hiyo.

decisions.choice: those who say "let us do evil"
decisions.reason: "Whom" may refer to anyone who reasons this way, or to those who falsely accuse Paul. Either way the judgment on them is just.

decisions.choice: God will be right to condemn
decisions.reason: Readable names God as judge, as the whole passage speaks of God's judgment.

records.literal_gloss: What then?

en.L: What then?
en.B: What then?
en.R: So what does this mean?

es.L: ¿Qué, pues?
es.B: ¿Qué, entonces?
es.R: Entonces, ¿qué quiere decir esto?

fr.L: Quoi donc ?
fr.B: Quoi donc ?
fr.R: Alors, que faut-il en conclure ?

sw.L: Basi nini?
sw.B: Basi, ni nini?
sw.R: Basi, hii ina maana gani?

source.text: προεχόμεθα;

records.literal_gloss: Are we better off?

en.L: Are we better off?
en.B: Do we Jews have an advantage?
en.R: Are we Jews better off than others?

es.L: ¿Llevamos ventaja?
es.B: ¿Tenemos los judíos alguna ventaja?
es.R: ¿Estamos los judíos en mejor situación que los demás?

fr.L: Avons-nous l’avantage ?
fr.B: Nous, les Juifs, avons-nous un avantage ?
fr.R: Nous, les Juifs, sommes-nous mieux placés que les autres ?

sw.L: Je, sisi tu bora zaidi?
sw.B: Je, sisi Wayahudi tuna ubora wowote?
sw.R: Je, sisi Wayahudi tuko katika hali bora kuliko wengine?

decisions.reason: προέχομαι is rare and its form unclear. Read as active in sense it asks "do we have an advantage?", which fits the answer that all are under sin. Read as middle it means "are we shielding ourselves?", and as passive "are we at a disadvantage?". "We" is most likely the Jews, with whom Paul counts himself.
Balanced and Readable say who "we" are.

source.text: οὐ πάντως, προῃτιασάμεθα γὰρ Ἰουδαίους τε καὶ Ἕλληνας πάντας ὑφ’ ἁμαρτίαν εἶναι, καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Οὐκ ἔστιν δίκαιος οὐδὲ εἷς, οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ συνίων, οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ ἐκζητῶν τὸν θεόν·

records.literal_gloss: Not at all; we already charged for Jews both and Greeks all under sin to be, \v 10 as it has been written that: There is not righteous not even one, \v 11 there is not the [one] understanding, there is not the [one] seeking out the God;

en.L: Not at all, for we have already charged that both Jews and Greeks are all under sin, \v 10 just as it is written: "There is no one righteous, not even one; \v 11 there is no one who understands; there is no one who seeks God;"
en.B: Not at all. We have already brought the charge that all, Jews and Greeks alike, are under the power of sin. \v 10 As it is written, "No one is righteous, not even one. \v 11 No one understands; no one seeks God."
en.R: No, not at all. We have already shown that all people are under the power of sin, both Jews and non-Jews. \v 10 The Scriptures say, "No one is righteous, not even one person. \v 11 No one understands. No one looks for God."

es.L: No, en absoluto; porque ya hemos acusado tanto a judíos como a griegos de estar todos bajo [el] pecado, \v 10 así como está escrito: «No hay [nadie] justo, ni siquiera uno; \v 11 no hay quien entienda; no hay quien busque a Dios».
es.B: No, en absoluto. Ya hemos presentado la acusación de que todos, judíos y griegos por igual, están bajo el poder del pecado. \v 10 Como está escrito: «Nadie es justo, ni uno solo. \v 11 Nadie entiende; nadie busca a Dios».
es.R: No, en absoluto. Ya hemos mostrado que todas las personas están bajo el poder del pecado, tanto los judíos como los que no son judíos. \v 10 Las Escrituras dicen: «Nadie es justo, ni una sola persona. \v 11 Nadie entiende. Nadie busca a Dios».

fr.L: Pas du tout, car nous avons déjà accusé Juifs et Grecs d’être tous sous le péché, \v 10 selon qu’il est écrit : « Il n’y a aucun juste, pas même un ; \v 11 il n’y a personne qui comprenne, il n’y a personne qui recherche Dieu ; »
fr.B: Pas du tout. Nous avons déjà porté l’accusation : tous, Juifs comme Grecs, sont sous la puissance du péché. \v 10 Comme il est écrit : « Personne n’est juste, pas même un seul. \v 11 Personne ne comprend ; personne ne cherche Dieu. »
fr.R: Non, pas du tout. Nous avons déjà montré que tout le monde est sous la puissance du péché, les Juifs comme les non-Juifs. \v 10 Les Écritures disent : « Personne n’est juste, pas une seule personne. \v 11 Personne ne comprend. Personne ne cherche Dieu. »

sw.L: Hapana kabisa; kwa maana tumekwisha kuwashtaki Wayahudi na Wagiriki kwamba wote wako chini ya dhambi, \v 10 kama ilivyoandikwa: "Hakuna aliye mwenye haki, hapana hata mmoja; \v 11 hakuna anayeelewa; hakuna anayemtafuta Mungu."
sw.B: Hapana kabisa. Tumekwisha kutoa mashtaka kwamba wote, Wayahudi na Wagiriki vilevile, wako chini ya nguvu ya dhambi. \v 10 Kama ilivyoandikwa, "Hakuna mtu aliye mwenye haki, hakuna hata mmoja. \v 11 Hakuna anayeelewa; hakuna anayemtafuta Mungu."
sw.R: Hapana, hata kidogo. Tumekwisha kuonyesha kwamba watu wote wako chini ya nguvu ya dhambi, Wayahudi na watu wasio Wayahudi pia. \v 10 Maandiko yanasema, "Hakuna mtu aliye mwenye haki, hata mtu mmoja. \v 11 Hakuna anayeelewa. Hakuna anayemtafuta Mungu."

decisions.reason: "Under sin" is under its rule, as a slave is under a master (7:14). Sin in Romans is a power, not only a list of wrong acts.
προαιτιάομαι is a law-court word, to bring a charge beforehand: Paul has made the case in 1:18-2:29.

Verses 10-18 string together lines from the Psalms and Isaiah. Verses 10-12 follow Psalm 14:1-3 (also Psalm 53:2-4). "No one is righteous" puts in Paul's own word what the psalm says as "no one does good" (compare Ecclesiastes 7:20).
Balanced and Readable say what "under" means, as the meaning decision explains.
As in 1:16.

source.text: πάντες ἐξέκλιναν, ἅμα ἠχρεώθησαν· οὐκ ἔστιν ποιῶν χρηστότητα, οὐκ ἔστιν ἕως ἑνός.

records.literal_gloss: All turned aside, together became worthless; there is not [one] doing kindness, there is not up to one.

en.L: "All have turned aside; together they have become worthless; there is no one who does good, there is not even one."
en.B: "All have turned away; together they have become useless. No one does what is good, not a single one."
en.R: "All of them have turned away from God. All of them have become worthless. No one does what is good, not even one person."

es.L: «Todos se desviaron, a una se volvieron inútiles; no hay quien haga lo bueno, no hay ni siquiera uno».
es.B: «Todos se han apartado; juntos se han echado a perder. Nadie hace el bien, ni uno solo».
es.R: «Todos se han alejado de Dios. Todos se han vuelto inútiles. Nadie hace lo bueno, ni una sola persona».

fr.L: « Tous ont dévié, ensemble ils sont devenus sans valeur ; il n’y a personne qui fasse le bien, il n’y en a pas même un. »
fr.B: « Tous se sont détournés ; ensemble, ils sont devenus inutiles. Personne ne fait le bien, pas un seul. »
fr.R: « Tous se sont détournés de Dieu. Tous sont devenus bons à rien. Personne ne fait ce qui est bien, pas même une seule personne. »

sw.L: "Wote wamegeuka kando, kwa pamoja wamekuwa hawafai; hakuna anayetenda wema, hakuna hata mmoja."
sw.B: "Wote wamegeuka mbali; kwa pamoja wameharibika. Hakuna anayetenda mema, hakuna hata mmoja."
sw.R: "Wote wamemwacha Mungu. Wote wamekuwa hawafai kitu. Hakuna anayetenda mema, hata mtu mmoja."

decisions.reason: The quotation continues Psalm 14:3.
ἀχρειόομαι is to become useless, like something spoiled; the psalm's Hebrew word means "gone sour" or "corrupt".
Readable says from whom they turned.

source.text: τάφος ἀνεῳγμένος ὁ λάρυγξ αὐτῶν, ταῖς γλώσσαις αὐτῶν ἐδολιοῦσαν, ἰὸς ἀσπίδων ὑπὸ τὰ χείλη αὐτῶν, ὧν τὸ στόμα ἀρᾶς καὶ πικρίας γέμει·

records.literal_gloss: A grave having been opened the throat of them, with the tongues of them they deceived, venom of asps under the lips of them, \v 14 of whom the mouth of cursing and of bitterness is full;

en.L: "Their throat [is] an opened grave; with their tongues they deceive; [the] venom of vipers [is] under their lips; \v 14 their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness;"
en.B: "Their throat is a grave left open; with their tongues they deal in deceit. Snake venom lies behind their lips. \v 14 Their mouths overflow with cursing and bitter words."
en.R: "What they say is like the stink from an open grave. They use their tongues to lie. Their words are as deadly as snake poison. \v 14 Their mouths are always cursing and saying bitter things."

es.L: «Sepulcro abierto [es] su garganta; con sus lenguas engañan; veneno de víboras [hay] bajo sus labios; \v 14 su boca está llena de maldición y amargura».
es.B: «Su garganta es una tumba que quedó abierta; con la lengua tejen engaños. Hay veneno de serpiente tras sus labios. \v 14 Su boca rebosa de maldiciones y palabras amargas».
es.R: «Lo que dicen es como el mal olor de una tumba abierta. Usan la lengua para mentir. Sus palabras son tan mortales como el veneno de serpiente. \v 14 Su boca siempre está maldiciendo y diciendo cosas amargas».

fr.L: « Leur gorge [est] une tombe ouverte ; avec leurs langues ils trompent ; le venin des vipères [est] sous leurs lèvres ; \v 14 leur bouche est remplie de malédiction et d’amertume ; »
fr.B: « Leur gorge est une tombe béante ; de leur langue, ils trompent. Un venin de serpent se cache derrière leurs lèvres. \v 14 Leur bouche déborde de malédictions et de paroles amères. »
fr.R: « Ce qu’ils disent est comme la puanteur d’une tombe ouverte. Ils se servent de leur langue pour mentir. Leurs paroles sont aussi mortelles que du venin de serpent. \v 14 Ils passent leur temps à maudire et à dire des paroles amères. »

sw.L: "Koo lao [ni] kaburi lililo wazi; kwa ndimi zao wanadanganya; sumu ya nyoka [iko] chini ya midomo yao; \v 14 kinywa chao kimejawa na kulaani na uchungu."
sw.B: "Koo lao ni kama kaburi lililoachwa wazi; kwa ndimi zao wanafanya hila. Sumu ya nyoka imejificha nyuma ya midomo yao. \v 14 Vinywa vyao vinafurika maneno ya laana na ya uchungu."
sw.R: "Maneno yao ni kama harufu mbaya ya kaburi lililo wazi. Wanatumia ndimi zao kudanganya. Maneno yao yanaua kama sumu ya nyoka. \v 14 Vinywa vyao daima vinalaani na kusema maneno ya uchungu."

decisions.reason: Verse 13 begins with Psalm 5:10.
"Venom of vipers under their lips" is from Psalm 140:4.
Verse 14 is from Psalm 10:7.

decisions.choice: an open grave: speech that brings death
decisions.reason: An open grave gives off the smell of death and waits to be filled. Their throats, the source of their words, are like that.

decisions.choice: like the stink from an open grave; as deadly as snake poison
decisions.reason: Readable turns the pictures into comparisons and says they are about speech.

source.text: ὀξεῖς οἱ πόδες αὐτῶν ἐκχέαι αἷμα, σύντριμμα καὶ ταλαιπωρία ἐν ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν, καὶ ὁδὸν εἰρήνης οὐκ ἔγνωσαν.

records.literal_gloss: Swift the feet of them to shed blood, \v 16 ruin and misery in the ways of them, \v 17 and way of peace not they knew.

en.L: "Their feet [are] swift to shed blood; \v 16 ruin and misery [are] in their paths, \v 17 and [the] way of peace they have not known."
en.B: "They rush to shed blood; \v 16 wherever they go they leave ruin and misery, \v 17 and the way of peace they have never known."
en.R: "They are quick to kill people. \v 16 Wherever they go, they destroy things and make people suffer. \v 17 They do not know how to live in peace."

es.L: «Sus pies [son] veloces para derramar sangre; \v 16 destrucción y miseria [hay] en sus caminos, \v 17 y camino de paz no han conocido».
es.B: «Corren a derramar sangre; \v 16 por dondequiera que van dejan ruina y miseria, \v 17 y nunca han conocido el camino de la paz».
es.R: «Están siempre listos para matar. \v 16 Por donde pasan, destruyen y hacen sufrir a la gente. \v 17 No saben vivir en paz».

fr.L: « Leurs pieds [sont] rapides pour verser le sang ; \v 16 la ruine et le malheur [sont] sur leurs chemins, \v 17 et le chemin de la paix, ils ne [l’]ont pas connu. »
fr.B: « Ils courent verser le sang ; \v 16 partout où ils passent, ils laissent ruine et misère, \v 17 et le chemin de la paix, ils ne l’ont jamais connu. »
fr.R: « Ils sont toujours prêts à tuer. \v 16 Partout où ils vont, ils détruisent et font souffrir les gens. \v 17 Ils ne savent pas vivre en paix. »

sw.L: "Miguu yao [ni] myepesi kumwaga damu; \v 16 uharibifu na taabu [viko] katika njia zao, \v 17 na njia ya amani hawajaijua."
sw.B: "Wanakimbilia kumwaga damu; \v 16 popote waendapo huacha maangamizi na dhiki, \v 17 nao hawajawahi kuijua njia ya amani."
sw.R: "Wana haraka ya kuua watu. \v 16 Popote wanapokwenda, wanaharibu vitu na kuwatesa watu. \v 17 Hawajui jinsi ya kuishi kwa amani."

decisions.reason: Verses 15-17 shorten Isaiah 59:7-8, which describes Israel's own sin; "their feet run to shed blood" is also in Proverbs 1:16.
Swift feet are eagerness: they are quick to violence.

decisions.choice: quick to kill people; how to live in peace
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the pictures of feet and ways mean.

source.text: οὐκ ἔστιν φόβος θεοῦ ἀπέναντι τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: There is not fear of God before the eyes of them.

en.L: "There is no fear of God before their eyes."
en.B: "The fear of God is nowhere in their sight."
en.R: "They do not respect God or fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

es.L: «No hay temor de Dios ante sus ojos».
es.B: «No tienen a la vista el temor de Dios».
es.R: «No respetan a Dios ni {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} temen».

fr.L: « Il n’y a pas de crainte de Dieu devant leurs yeux. »
fr.B: « Ils n’ont jamais devant les yeux la crainte de Dieu. »
fr.R: « Ils ne respectent pas Dieu et ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} craignent pas. »

sw.L: "Hakuna kumcha Mungu mbele ya macho yao."
sw.B: "Kumcha Mungu hakuonekani popote machoni pao."
sw.R: "Hawamheshimu Mungu wala hawamchi."

decisions.reason: The last line is from Psalm 36:2.

decisions.choice: the fear of God: reverence for God
decisions.reason: In the Bible the fear of God is the awe and reverence that shapes how a person lives (Proverbs 1:7). "Before their eyes" means in their thoughts and choices.
The fear of God is the reverence that shapes a life (meaning decision). Swahili has a verb for exactly that, "kumcha Mungu"; "hofu" is being afraid, which would narrow it to terror.

source.text: Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι ὅσα ὁ νόμος λέγει τοῖς ἐν τῷ νόμῳ λαλεῖ, ἵνα πᾶν στόμα φραγῇ καὶ ὑπόδικος γένηται πᾶς ὁ κόσμος τῷ θεῷ·

records.literal_gloss: We know now that whatever the law says to those in the law it speaks, so that every mouth may be shut and accountable may become all the world to the God;

en.L: Now we know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those who are in the law, so that every mouth may be shut and the whole world may become accountable to God;
en.B: We know that what the law says is addressed to those who live under the law. It is said so that every mouth will be closed and the whole world will stand accountable to God.
en.R: We know that what the law says is spoken to those who have the law. It says this so that no one can make any excuse, and so that the whole world must answer to God.

es.L: Ahora bien, sabemos que todo lo que la ley dice, lo dice a los que [están] en la ley, para que toda boca sea cerrada y todo el mundo llegue a ser responsable ante Dios;
es.B: Sabemos que lo que dice la ley va dirigido a los que viven bajo la ley. Se dice para que toda boca quede cerrada y el mundo entero tenga que rendir cuentas a Dios.
es.R: Sabemos que lo que dice la ley es para los que tienen la ley. Lo dice para que nadie pueda poner excusas, y para que el mundo entero tenga que responder ante Dios.

fr.L: Or nous savons que tout ce que dit la Loi, elle le dit à ceux qui sont dans la Loi, afin que toute bouche soit fermée et que le monde entier soit tenu de rendre compte à Dieu ;
fr.B: Nous savons que ce que dit la Loi s’adresse à ceux qui vivent sous la Loi. Elle le dit pour que toute bouche soit fermée et que le monde entier ait à rendre des comptes à Dieu.
fr.R: Nous savons que ce que dit la Loi est dit à ceux qui ont la Loi. Elle le dit pour que personne ne puisse trouver d’excuse, et pour que le monde entier doive répondre devant Dieu.

sw.L: Basi tunajua kwamba yote ambayo sheria inasema, inawaambia wale walio katika sheria, ili kila kinywa kizibwe na ulimwengu wote uwajibike mbele za Mungu;
sw.B: Tunajua kwamba yale ambayo sheria inasema yanawahusu wale wanaoishi chini ya sheria. Yamesemwa ili kila kinywa kinyamaze, na ulimwengu wote uwajibike mbele za Mungu.
sw.R: Tunajua kwamba yale ambayo sheria inasema yanawahusu wale walio na sheria. Inasema hivyo ili mtu yeyote asiwe na kisingizio, na ili ulimwengu wote ulazimike kujieleza mbele za Mungu.

decisions.choice: the law: the Scriptures as a whole
alternatives: the five books of Moses only
decisions.reason: The quotations in verses 10-18 come from the Psalms and Isaiah, yet Paul calls them "the law". Here the word covers all of Israel's Scriptures.

decisions.choice: every mouth shut: no defense left
decisions.reason: In a court, the accused who has no answer falls silent. ὑπόδικος is a legal word: answerable, liable to judgment.

decisions.choice: if those with the law are guilty, so is the whole world
decisions.reason: The Gentiles stand condemned already (1:18-32). If the Scriptures convict even those who have them, no one is left to plead innocence.

decisions.choice: no one can make any excuse
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means.

source.text: διότι ἐξ ἔργων νόμου οὐ δικαιωθήσεται πᾶσα σὰρξ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ, διὰ γὰρ νόμου ἐπίγνωσις ἁμαρτίας.

records.literal_gloss: Because from works of law not will be justified all flesh before him, through for law knowledge of sin.

en.L: because by works of [the] law no flesh will be justified before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, for through [the] law [comes] knowledge of sin.
en.B: No one will be declared righteous before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the basis of works of the law. What the law does is make sin known.
en.R: No one can be made right with God by doing what the law says. What the law does is show people their sin.

es.L: porque por [las] obras de [la] ley ninguna carne será justificada delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, pues por medio de [la] ley [viene el] conocimiento del pecado.
es.B: Nadie será justificado delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} por las obras de la ley. Lo que hace la ley es dar a conocer el pecado.
es.R: Dios no declara justo a nadie porque haga lo que la ley manda. Lo que hace la ley es mostrar a la gente su pecado.

fr.L: parce que par les œuvres de la Loi nulle chair ne sera justifiée devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, car par la Loi [vient] la connaissance du péché.
fr.B: Personne ne sera déclaré juste devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} sur la base des œuvres de la Loi. Ce que fait la Loi, c’est faire connaître le péché.
fr.R: Personne ne peut être mis en règle avec Dieu en faisant ce que dit la Loi. Ce que fait la Loi, c’est montrer aux gens leur péché.

sw.L: kwa sababu kwa matendo ya sheria hakuna mwili utakaohesabiwa haki mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kwa maana kupitia sheria [huja] kuitambua dhambi.
sw.B: Hakuna mtu atakayehesabiwa haki mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa matendo ya sheria. Kazi ya sheria ni kuifanya dhambi itambulike.
sw.R: Hakuna mtu anayeweza kuhesabiwa haki na Mungu kwa kufanya yale ambayo sheria inasema. Kazi ya sheria ni kuwaonyesha watu dhambi yao.

decisions.reason: Paul echoes Psalm 143:2, "no one living is righteous before you", and adds "by works of the law" (as in Galatians 2:16).

decisions.choice: works of the law: what the law requires
alternatives: the parts of the law that marked Jews out, such as circumcision, food laws and the Sabbath
decisions.reason: "Works of the law" are deeds done in obedience to the law of Moses. Some readers stress the commands that set Jews apart from Gentiles, which the letter does discuss (2:25-29, 3:29-30, 14:1-6); others take the phrase to cover everything the law requires. Either way, no one is declared righteous on that basis.
"Flesh" here is a Hebrew way of saying human beings in their weakness.

decisions.choice: knowledge of sin: recognition of it as sin
decisions.reason: ἐπίγνωσις is knowledge that recognizes. The law shows sin for what it is (7:7).

"Matendo" (deeds) says that these are things done in obedience to the law, as the meaning decision explains; "kazi" would suggest labour or a job. The phrase returns in verses 27-28 and keeps this form there.

source.text: Νυνὶ δὲ χωρὶς νόμου δικαιοσύνη θεοῦ πεφανέρωται, μαρτυρουμένη ὑπὸ τοῦ νόμου καὶ τῶν προφητῶν, δικαιοσύνη δὲ θεοῦ διὰ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, εἰς πάντας τοὺς πιστεύοντας, οὐ γάρ ἐστιν διαστολή.

records.literal_gloss: Now but apart from law righteousness of God has been made known, being witnessed by the law and the prophets, \v 22 righteousness and of God through faith of Jesus Christ for all the [ones] believing; not for is distinction.

en.L: But now apart from [the] law [the] righteousness of God has been made known, being witnessed by the Law and the Prophets, \v 22 [the] righteousness of God through faith in Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} for all who believe. For there is no distinction.
en.B: But now God's righteousness has come to light apart from the law, though the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it. \v 22 It is God's righteousness through faith in Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, for all who believe. No one is treated differently.
en.R: But now God has shown {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness, how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} puts people right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done it without the law. The Law and the Prophets in the Scriptures spoke about this long ago. \v 22 God puts people right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} through faith in Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. He does this for everyone who believes. Everyone is the same.

es.L: Pero ahora, aparte de [la] ley, [la] justicia de Dios ha sido manifestada, siendo atestiguada por la Ley y los Profetas, \v 22 [la] justicia de Dios por medio de [la] fe en {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, para todos los que creen. Porque no hay distinción.
es.B: Pero ahora la justicia de Dios se ha dado a conocer sin la ley, aunque la Ley y los Profetas dan testimonio de ella. \v 22 Es la justicia de Dios por medio de la fe en {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, para todos los que creen. Nadie recibe un trato distinto.
es.R: Pero ahora Dios ha mostrado {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} justicia: cómo pone a las personas en una relación correcta con {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}}. Y lo ha hecho sin la ley. La Ley y los Profetas, en las Escrituras, ya hablaban de esto hace mucho tiempo. \v 22 Dios pone a las personas en una relación correcta con {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}} por medio de la fe en {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Lo hace con todos los que creen. Todos son iguales.

fr.L: Mais maintenant, en dehors de la Loi, la justice de Dieu a été manifestée, attestée par la Loi et les Prophètes, \v 22 la justice de Dieu par la foi en Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} pour tous ceux qui croient. Car il n’y a pas de différence.
fr.B: Mais maintenant, la justice de Dieu est apparue en dehors de la Loi, même si la Loi et les Prophètes en rendent témoignage. \v 22 C’est la justice de Dieu par la foi en Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, pour tous ceux qui croient. Personne n’est traité différemment.
fr.R: Mais maintenant, Dieu a montré {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} justice, la manière dont {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} met les gens en règle avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a fait sans la Loi. La Loi et les Prophètes, dans les Écritures, en avaient parlé il y a longtemps. \v 22 Dieu met les gens en règle avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} par la foi en Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. Il le fait pour tous ceux qui croient. Tous sont pareils.

sw.L: Lakini sasa, bila sheria, haki ya Mungu imeonyeshwa wazi, ikishuhudiwa na Sheria na Manabii, \v 22 haki ya Mungu kupitia imani katika Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kwa ajili ya wote wanaoamini. Kwa maana hakuna tofauti.
sw.B: Lakini sasa haki ya Mungu imeonyeshwa wazi bila sheria, ingawa Maandiko ya Sheria na Manabii yanaishuhudia. \v 22 Ni haki ya Mungu kupitia imani katika Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kwa ajili ya wote wanaoamini. Hakuna anayetendewa tofauti.
sw.R: Lakini sasa Mungu ameonyesha haki {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}: jinsi anavyowaweka watu katika uhusiano mwema naye {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}. Amefanya hivyo bila sheria. Maandiko ya Sheria na Manabii yalisema habari hii zamani sana. \v 22 Mungu anawaweka watu katika uhusiano mwema naye {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} kupitia imani katika Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Anafanya hivyo kwa kila mtu anayeamini. Wote ni sawa.

decisions.reason: "But now" marks the time God has acted in Christ, after the long account of human guilt (1:18-3:20).

decisions.choice: apart from the law: not by keeping the law
decisions.reason: God's righteousness has come without the law as its means, though the law itself bears witness to it.

decisions.choice: the Law and the Prophets: the Scriptures
decisions.reason: A Jewish name for the Scriptures, from two of their parts. Chapter 4 shows the witness of Genesis and the Psalms.

The phrase is literally "faith of Jesus Christ". It can mean the faith that has Jesus as its object, or Jesus' own faithfulness to God, shown in his death. "For all who believe" in the same verse speaks of human faith, and Galatians 2:16 joins the phrase to "we believed in Christ Jesus". The levels follow the first reading; the second is held by many.
See 1:17: God acting rightly to put people right with himself.

decisions.choice: no distinction between Jew and Gentile
decisions.reason: διαστολή is a difference or distinction; here between Jew and Greek, as 10:12 says.
Title setting.

decisions.choice: how he puts people right with himself
decisions.reason: As in 1:17.

The meaning decision reads the phrase as faith that has Jesus as its object, and its footnote gives his own faithfulness as the other reading. Spanish "la fe de Jesucristo", the older wording, copies the Greek's ambiguity but is usually heard as the faith Jesus himself had; "fe en" says what the meaning decision chooses. Verse 26 uses the same wording ("fe en Jesús").

decisions.choice: ha sido manifestada (L); se ha dado a conocer (B)
decisions.reason: This is a different verb from the one in 1:17, where the righteousness of God "se revela". "Manifestar" says that it has been brought into the open, and keeps the two verbs apart.

decisions.choice: cómo pone a las personas en una relación correcta con {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}}
decisions.reason: Readable explains God's righteousness in the same words as 1:17 and 10:3, so a reader can follow the term through the letter. The verb "justificar" is explained at Readable as "declarar justo" (verses 24, 26, 28 and 30), as settled at 2:13.

"Imani ya Yesu Kristo" would copy the Greek's ambiguity, but Swahili "ya" is most naturally heard as the faith Jesus has. The meaning decision reads the phrase as faith in Jesus, so Swahili says "imani katika"; the footnote on the meaning decision gives the other reading. Verse 26 uses the same wording ("imani katika Yesu").
This is a different verb from 1:17 ("inafunuliwa", is revealed): this one means brought into the open. "Imeonyeshwa wazi" (has been shown openly) keeps the two apart.

A Jewish name for the Scriptures (meaning decision), capitalised as in the English. "Torati" is the familiar name for the books of Moses, but "Sheria" is the same word as "bila sheria" earlier in the verse, so the reader sees that the law itself bears witness. Balanced and Readable say "Maandiko ya Sheria na Manabii" (the writings of the Law and the Prophets), which also gives the verb a natural agreement.

source.text: πάντες γὰρ ἥμαρτον καὶ ὑστεροῦνται τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ, δικαιούμενοι δωρεὰν τῇ αὐτοῦ χάριτι διὰ τῆς ἀπολυτρώσεως τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: All for sinned and fall short of the glory of the God, \v 24 being justified as a gift by the of him grace through the redemption the [one] in Christ Jesus;

en.L: For all sinned and are lacking the glory of God, \v 24 being justified as a gift by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace through the redemption that is in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus;
en.B: Everyone has sinned, and all come short of God's glory. \v 24 Yet they are declared righteous as a free gift, by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, through the redemption found in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.
en.R: Everyone has sinned. No one has the glory God meant people to have. \v 24 But God puts people right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} as a free gift, because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace. {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} Jesus paid the price to set them free.

es.L: Porque todos pecaron y carecen de la gloria de Dios, \v 24 siendo justificados como un regalo por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia, por medio de la redención que [está] en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}};
es.B: Todos han pecado, y a todos les falta la gloria de Dios. \v 24 Pero, como un regalo, son justificados por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia, por medio de la redención que se encuentra en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}.
es.R: Todos han pecado. Nadie tiene la gloria que Dios quiso que las personas tuvieran. \v 24 Pero Dios, por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia, declara justas a las personas como un regalo. {{christos:Cristo Jesús|El Mesías Jesús}} pagó el rescate para dejarlas libres.

fr.L: Car tous ont péché et restent en manque de la gloire de Dieu, \v 24 étant justifiés à titre de don par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce, à travers la rédemption qui est {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus ;
fr.B: Tous ont péché, et tous restent loin de la gloire de Dieu. \v 24 Pourtant, ils sont déclarés justes gratuitement, par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce, au moyen de la rédemption qui se trouve {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus.
fr.R: Tout le monde a péché. Personne n’a la gloire que Dieu voulait donner aux humains. \v 24 Mais Dieu met les gens en règle avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} gratuitement, à cause de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce. Le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus a payé le prix pour les libérer.

sw.L: Kwa maana wote walitenda dhambi, nao wanakosa utukufu wa Mungu, \v 24 wakihesabiwa haki kama zawadi kwa neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kupitia ukombozi ulio ndani ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu;
sw.B: Wote wametenda dhambi, na wote wanaukosa utukufu wa Mungu. \v 24 Lakini wanahesabiwa haki kama zawadi, bila malipo, kwa neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kupitia ukombozi unaopatikana katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.
sw.R: Kila mtu ametenda dhambi. Hakuna aliye na utukufu ambao Mungu alikusudia watu wawe nao. \v 24 Lakini kwa neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, Mungu anawahesabia watu haki kama zawadi ya bure. {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu alilipa gharama ya kuwakomboa, wawe huru.

decisions.choice: all sinned, and all go on falling short
decisions.reason: "Sinned" sums up the past; "fall short" is present: they lack the glory of God now.

decisions.choice: the glory of God: the glory people were made to share
decisions.reason: Human beings were made in God's image and crowned with glory (Psalm 8:6). Sin has left them without it; Paul says believers will share it again (5:2, 8:18-30).

decisions.choice: being justified: the same "all" who believe
decisions.reason: The participle joins loosely to what comes before: those who all sinned are, as they believe (verse 22), declared righteous.
δωρεάν is "without payment": nothing is paid for it.

decisions.choice: redemption: setting free by a payment
decisions.reason: ἀπολύτρωσις is release, especially of a slave or captive by paying a price. It recalls God freeing Israel from Egypt. Paul does not say here to whom a price is paid.
Title setting.

decisions.choice: paid the price to set them free
decisions.reason: Readable explains redemption, as the meaning decision describes it.
"Gratuitamente" is the older word, but in everyday Spanish it can also mean "for no reason". "Como un regalo" says what the meaning decision describes: nothing is paid for it.

decisions.choice: redención (L, B); pagó el rescate para dejarlas libres (R)
decisions.reason: "Redención" is the settled word for the letter. Readable explains it with "rescate", the price paid to free a captive, as the meaning decision describes it, without saying to whom it is paid.

alternatives: pone a las personas en una relación correcta con él mismo
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable says "puts people right with himself" for the verb, Spanish Readable says "declarar justo", as settled at 2:13, and keeps the longer explanation for the noun "justicia" (verse 21).

decisions.choice: "{{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus" for "in Christ Jesus"
decisions.reason: As set at 1:1: French cannot say "en Messie", so the span covers the preposition, while the English span covers the title alone.

decisions.choice: ukombozi (L, B); alilipa gharama ya kuwakomboa (R)
decisions.reason: "Ukombozi" is the settled word; it belongs with "kukomboa", to buy back or set free a captive, which is the sense the meaning decision gives. Readable keeps the verb and says that a price was paid, without saying to whom.

alternatives: Mungu anawaweka watu katika uhusiano mwema naye
decisions.reason: As settled at 2:13, "kuhesabiwa haki" is kept at every level. Readable uses the active "Mungu anawahesabia watu haki" (God counts people righteous) where the English Readable says "puts people right with himself", and keeps that longer explanation for the noun "haki ya Mungu" (verse 21).

source.text: ὃν προέθετο ὁ θεὸς ἱλαστήριον διὰ πίστεως ἐν τῷ αὐτοῦ αἵματι εἰς ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτοῦ διὰ τὴν πάρεσιν τῶν προγεγονότων ἁμαρτημάτων ἐν τῇ ἀνοχῇ τοῦ θεοῦ, πρὸς τὴν ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν δίκαιον καὶ δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἐκ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: whom set forth the God atonement through faith in the of him blood for demonstration of the righteousness of him because of the passing over of the having happened before sins \v 26 in the forbearance of the God, for the demonstration of the righteousness of him in the now time, for the to be him righteous and justifying the [one] from faith of Jesus.

en.L: whom God put forward as a means of atonement, through faith, by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood, for a demonstration of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness, because of the passing over of sins committed beforehand \v 26 in the forbearance of God, for the demonstration of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness at the present time, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might be righteous and the one who justifies the one [who has] faith in Jesus.
en.B: God put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} forward as the means of atonement, by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood, to be received through faith. He did this to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness, since {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had passed over the sins committed before, \v 26 when God held back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgment. He did it to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness at the present time, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would be righteous and also the one who declares righteous whoever has faith in Jesus.
en.R: God offered Jesus as the sacrifice that takes away sins and turns away God's anger. Jesus did this by shedding {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood, and people receive it through faith. God did this to show that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is righteous, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had let earlier sins go unpunished \v 26 while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was patient. Now God shows {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness. He shows that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is righteous, and that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} puts right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} everyone who has faith in Jesus.

es.L: a quien Dios presentó públicamente como medio de expiación, por medio de [la] fe, por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sangre, para demostración de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} justicia, a causa de haber pasado por alto los pecados cometidos anteriormente \v 26 en la tolerancia de Dios, para demostración de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} justicia en el tiempo presente, a fin de que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sea justo y el que justifica al que [tiene] fe en Jesús.
es.B: Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} presentó públicamente como medio de expiación, por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sangre, para que se reciba por medio de la fe. Lo hizo para mostrar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} justicia, porque había pasado por alto los pecados cometidos antes, \v 26 cuando Dios contuvo {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} juicio. Lo hizo para mostrar {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} justicia en el tiempo presente, para ser {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} justo y, a la vez, el que justifica a todo el que tiene fe en Jesús.
es.R: Dios ofreció a Jesús como el sacrificio que quita los pecados y aparta la ira de Dios. Jesús lo hizo derramando {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sangre, y las personas lo reciben por medio de la fe. Dios hizo esto para mostrar que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es justo, porque antes había dejado sin castigo los pecados de la gente \v 26 mientras tenía paciencia. Ahora Dios muestra {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} justicia. Muestra que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es justo, y que declara justo a todo el que tiene fe en Jesús.

fr.L: {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que Dieu a présenté comme moyen d’expiation, par la foi, par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sang, pour une démonstration de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} justice, du fait qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait laissé passer les péchés commis auparavant \v 26 dans la patience de Dieu, pour la démonstration de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} justice dans le temps présent, afin d’être juste et de justifier celui qui [a] la foi en Jésus.
fr.B: Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a présenté comme le moyen d’expiation, par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sang, à recevoir par la foi. Il l’a fait pour montrer {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} justice, puisqu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait laissé passer les péchés commis auparavant, \v 26 au temps où Dieu retenait {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} jugement. Il l’a fait pour montrer {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} justice dans le temps présent, afin d’être juste, et d’être aussi celui qui déclare juste quiconque a foi en Jésus.
fr.R: Dieu a offert Jésus comme le sacrifice qui enlève les péchés et détourne la colère de Dieu. Jésus l’a fait en versant {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sang, et les gens reçoivent ce sacrifice par la foi. Dieu a fait cela pour montrer qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est juste, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait laissé sans punition les péchés d’autrefois \v 26 pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se montrait patient. Maintenant, Dieu montre {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} justice. Il montre qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est juste, et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} met en règle avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} tous ceux qui ont foi en Jésus.

sw.L: ambaye Mungu alimweka hadharani kuwa njia ya upatanisho, kupitia imani, kwa damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, ili kuonyesha haki {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kwa sababu ya kuziacha [bila adhabu] dhambi zilizotendwa hapo awali \v 26 katika uvumilivu wa Mungu, ili kuonyesha haki {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} katika wakati huu wa sasa, ili {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} awe mwenye haki, na anayemhesabia haki yule [aliye] na imani katika Yesu.
sw.B: Mungu alimweka {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hadharani kuwa njia ya upatanisho, kwa damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, ipokewe kwa imani. Alifanya hivyo ili kuonyesha haki {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kwa kuwa alikuwa ameziacha bila adhabu dhambi zilizotendwa zamani, \v 26 wakati Mungu alipoizuia hukumu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Alifanya hivyo ili kuonyesha haki {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} wakati huu wa sasa, ili {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} awe mwenye haki, na pia awe yule anayemhesabia haki kila mtu aliye na imani katika Yesu.
sw.R: Mungu alimtoa Yesu kuwa dhabihu inayoondoa dhambi na kuigeuza mbali ghadhabu ya Mungu. Yesu alifanya hivyo kwa kumwaga damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na watu wanaipokea dhabihu hiyo kwa imani. Mungu alifanya hivi ili kuonyesha kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mwenye haki, kwa sababu zamani aliziacha dhambi za watu bila kuziadhibu \v 26 wakati alipokuwa akivumilia. Sasa Mungu anaonyesha haki {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Anaonyesha kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mwenye haki, na kwamba anamhesabia haki kila mtu aliye na imani katika Yesu.

decisions.choice: the means of atonement, the reality the mercy seat stood for
alternatives: a sacrifice that turns away God's wrath (propitiation)
a sacrifice that wipes away sin (expiation)
decisions.reason: ἱλαστήριον is the word the Greek translation of the Old Testament uses for the cover of the ark, the "mercy seat", where blood was sprinkled on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:14-15; Hebrews 9:5 uses it the same way). It can also mean an atoning sacrifice. Atonement in the Old Testament both wipes away sin and turns away God's wrath, which Paul has spoken of since 1:18. The levels keep both.

decisions.choice: "through faith" and "by his blood" both go with the atonement
decisions.reason: The atonement is made by Christ's blood and received through faith. "Faith in his blood" is not Paul's way of speaking.
προτίθεμαι can mean to set before others or to intend. Set against the hidden mercy seat, God displayed Christ openly.

decisions.choice: passing over: letting sins go unpunished for a time
decisions.reason: πάρεσις is not the usual word for forgiveness. God held back the punishment sins deserved, which could make him seem unjust; the cross shows that he was not.

decisions.choice: God's righteousness: his justice and his saving action
decisions.reason: In verse 21 God's righteousness is his act of putting people right; here it is also his justice, shown because he did not ignore sin. Verse 26 holds both together: he is righteous, and he declares righteous.

decisions.choice: the one who has faith in Jesus
alternatives: the one who lives from Jesus' faithfulness
decisions.reason: The same question as "faith of Jesus Christ" in verse 22; see the note there.

decisions.choice: the sacrifice that takes away sins and turns away God's anger
decisions.reason: Readable spells out atonement, as the meaning decision describes it; reviewers should check that it does not narrow it.

decisions.choice: when God held back his judgment
decisions.reason: Balanced says what forbearance is, as in 2:4.

Spanish calls the Day of Atonement "el Día de la Expiación", so "expiación" is the Spanish word for atonement in the sense the meaning decision gives: what that day's sacrifice did, both wiping away sin and turning away God's wrath, and the reality the mercy seat stood for. "Propiciación", the older word, leans to one side only and is little known today; "propiciatorio" is the mercy seat itself, the meaning decision's first alternative. Readable explains both sides, as the English does. A reviewer should check that "expiación" is not heard as covering only the removal of sin.

decisions.choice: haber pasado por alto (L, B); dejar sin castigo (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads this word not as forgiveness but as God holding back the punishment sins deserved, for a time. "Remisión", the older Spanish wording, is heard as forgiveness, so Spanish says "pasar por alto" (overlook) and Readable "dejar sin castigo" (leave unpunished).
As in 2:4, "tolerancia" renders this word for God's holding back. Balanced explains it as the English does ("cuando Dios contuvo su juicio"), and Readable says "mientras tenía paciencia".

As the English "means of atonement", the French keeps open whether the word points to the mercy seat or to a sacrifice (m1). "Propitiatoire" names the lid of the ark but is unknown to most readers; "victime" would narrow the sense. Readable says what the atonement does, as the English Readable does.

"Upatanisho" is the Swahili word for atonement, as in "Siku ya Upatanisho" (the Day of Atonement, when blood was sprinkled on the mercy seat), so it keeps the link the meaning decision describes and covers both the wiping away of sin and the turning away of wrath. "Kiti cha rehema" (the mercy seat) is the meaning decision's first alternative; "kafara" is also heard as an offering to avert misfortune. The same root gives "kupatanisha" (to reconcile) in 5:10-11, which a reviewer should weigh. Readable explains both sides, as the English does.

"Kuachilia" is commonly heard as "to forgive", and the meaning decision says this word is not forgiveness but God holding back punishment for a time. "Kuziacha bila adhabu" (leaving them unpunished) says that; Literal brackets "bila adhabu" as words the Greek implies.
As in 2:4, "uvumilivu" (bearing with, holding back) renders this word. Balanced explains it as the English does ("alipoizuia hukumu yake"), and Readable says "alipokuwa akivumilia".

records.literal_gloss: No, but through law of faith.

en.L: No, but through [the] law of faith.

decisions.reason: νόμος is "law", but it can also mean a rule or principle. Paul may mean the principle of faith as against the principle of works, or the law of Moses itself, which, read rightly, points to faith (verse 31, 9:31-32).

source.text: λογιζόμεθα γὰρ δικαιοῦσθαι πίστει ἄνθρωπον χωρὶς ἔργων νόμου.

records.literal_gloss: We reckon for to be justified by faith a person apart from works of law.

en.L: For we hold that a {{gender:person|man}} is justified by faith apart from works of [the] law.
en.B: For we are convinced that a person is declared righteous by faith, apart from works of the law.
en.R: We are sure of this: God puts a person right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} through faith, not because the person has done what the law says.

es.L: Porque sostenemos que {{gender:el ser humano|el hombre}} es justificado por fe, aparte de [las] obras de [la] ley.
es.B: Porque estamos convencidos de que una persona es justificada por la fe, sin las obras de la ley.
es.R: Estamos seguros de esto: Dios declara justa a una persona por medio de la fe, no porque haya hecho lo que la ley manda.

fr.L: Car nous estimons qu’un {{gender:être humain|homme}} est justifié par la foi, sans les œuvres de la Loi.
fr.B: Car nous sommes convaincus qu’une personne est déclarée juste par la foi, sans les œuvres de la Loi.
fr.R: Nous en sommes sûrs : Dieu met une personne en règle avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} par la foi, et non parce qu’elle a fait ce que dit la Loi.

sw.L: Kwa maana tunahitimisha kwamba mtu huhesabiwa haki kwa imani bila matendo ya sheria.
sw.B: Kwa maana tuna hakika kwamba mtu anahesabiwa haki kwa imani, bila matendo ya sheria.
sw.R: Tuna uhakika na jambo hili: Mungu anamhesabia mtu haki kwa imani, wala si kwa sababu mtu huyo ametenda yale ambayo sheria inasema.

decisions.reason: λογίζομαι is to reckon, to reach a settled judgment; it is the word for "counted" in 4:3.

Many later manuscripts read "therefore", making the verse a conclusion; earlier ones read "for", giving the reason for verse 27. The SBLGNT reads "for". (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: by faith, apart from works of the law
decisions.reason: Faith is how a person is declared righteous; works of the law play no part in it (verse 20).
The word means a human being, man or woman.

Spanish follows the English setting. "El ser humano" rather than "una persona" lets the rest of the sentence stay the same in both options ("es justificado"), since "persona" would need feminine agreement outside the span.

fr.B: Oui, des non-Juifs aussi, \v 30 puisque Dieu est un. Il déclarera justes les circoncis par la foi, et les incirconcis par cette même foi.

decisions.reason: "The LORD our God, the LORD is one" (Deuteronomy 6:4) was recited daily by Jews. If there is one God, he is God of all peoples and puts all right in one way.

source.text: μὴ γένοιτο, ἀλλὰ νόμον ἱστάνομεν.

records.literal_gloss: May it not be, but law we establish.

en.L: May it not be! Rather, we establish [the] law.
en.B: Certainly not! On the contrary, we uphold the law.
en.R: Of course not! Instead, we give the law its rightful place.

es.L: ¡No sea así! Al contrario, establecemos [la] ley.
es.B: ¡De ningún modo! Al contrario, mantenemos firme la ley.
es.R: ¡Claro que no! Más bien, le damos a la ley el lugar que le corresponde.

sw.L: Isiwe hivyo! Bali tunaisimamisha sheria.
sw.B: Hasha! Badala yake, tunaitegemeza sheria.
sw.R: Sivyo kabisa! Badala yake, tunaipa sheria nafasi yake halali.

decisions.reason: μή in this form is a wish, "may it not come to be". Paul uses it to reject a false conclusion outright.

alternatives: the law's own witness to faith, shown in chapter 4
faith leads to doing what the law truly requires (8:4, 13:8-10)
decisions.reason: Paul does not say here how. In chapter 4 he shows that the law (Genesis) itself teaches righteousness by faith; later he says that those who walk by the Spirit fulfill what the law requires (8:4).

decisions.choice: May it not be! / Certainly not! / Of course not!
decisions.reason: Paul's strongest no, literally "may it not happen". The same English is used at each level wherever Romans has it (as in 9:14 and 11:1).
